subject: Multi-cloud geofencing & deletion — marketplace partner residency Q&A
messages:
From: Natalie Cheng <natalie@nimbusanalytics.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency + deletion questions for Marketplace listing

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this on. As we're prepping the Marketplace listing and the contract, our InfoSec team asked for a couple of concrete commitments we couldn't find in the standard docs. Can you confirm the following for Redwood when a customer selects region(s) during onboarding via the Marketplace flow (AWS/GCP/Azure):

- Exact zone/region mapping (e.g., us-east-1 vs us-east-2) — we need the list for EU/US/APAC for our legal clause.
- Deletion semantics: when a deletion request is made (via API or via our UI), how quickly does Redwood purge: serving cache, KV caches (LLM context), object store backups/snapshots, and any long-term cold backups?
- Does Redwood rely on cloud provider lifecycle rules (S3 lifecycle, GCS retention, Azure Blob) or does Redwood perform independent deletions across storage tiers?
- How does soft-delete/versioning in cloud buckets affect your guarantees (e.g., GCS object versioning or Azure soft-delete enabled by default)?
- Any special behavior for Marketplace-delivered Dedicated/Private deployments (snapshots, infra backups)?

Attached is our compliance checklist — some of these items map 1:1 to the questions above. If you can provide a short Q&A we can drop into the contract and the Marketplace listing page that would be super helpful.

Appreciate it,
Natalie
Natalie Cheng
Head of Platform Security
Nimbus Analytics

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Cheng <natalie@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency + deletion questions for Marketplace listing

Hi Natalie — thanks for the clear checklist. I broke answers down by topic and included next steps. I also attached a draft mapping spreadsheet for your review (residency_mapping_v1.xlsx).

1) Region mapping
- Marketplace onboarding supports explicit region pinning at account creation. For Marketplace (hosted) customers we map selections to the following canonical regions:
  - AWS: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-central-1, ap-southeast-1
  - GCP: us-central1, europe-west1, europe-west4, asia-south1
  - Azure: eastus, westus2, northeurope, westeurope, southeastasia
- If you need a strict ISO/locale mapping for contractual language, we can provide the exact region set per account in the deal paperwork (we recommend including "region set: AWS/GCP/Azure canonical list" as an appendix).

2) Deletion semantics (summary)
- Serving/cache: deletion request triggers immediate invalidation of serving-level caches and the in-memory KV (LLM context) for the tenant — typically within seconds.
- Object store (primary): Redwood issues deletion calls to the object store endpoint for the tenant-scoped objects. Primary object deletions are attempted immediately; most objects are deleted within minutes but completion varies by provider.
- Backups/snapshots/cold storage: Redwood runs a background removal workflow that removes backups and snapshots. For hosted Marketplace customers we commit to removing customer-accessible backups within 30 days after deletion by default. For dedicated/private deployments we can contract a shorter window (e.g., 7–14 days) as part of the Reserved Capacity terms.
- Cloud provider lifecycle quirks: if cloud provider versioning or soft-delete is enabled on the bucket, Redwood will coordinate the lifecycle action to ensure logical deletion within the committed SLA, but partner-managed buckets with versioning require partner confirmation to fully purge historical object versions.

3) Lifecycle vs Redwood-managed deletions
- Redwood executes independent deletions (we do not rely solely on customer-managed lifecycle rules). We operate a deletion workflow that calls provider APIs and validates object removal. We also reconcile against provider metadata to confirm the deletion. For extra assurance we surface a deletion-complete webhook/event customers can subscribe to.

4) Soft-delete / versioning implications
- GCS: If object versioning is enabled at the bucket level, object delete calls create a noncurrent generation; our workflow issues explicit delete calls for previous generations when we control the bucket. If the bucket is partner-managed and versioning is enabled, we flag this in the onboarding doc and recommend disabling versioning for data subject to deletion SLAs or agreeing to a longer purge window in contract.
- Azure Blob: Azure soft-delete (retention) must be disabled or set to an agreed value; otherwise soft-deleted blobs can persist beyond Redwood's deletion routine. We recommend a Marketplace contract clause that the partner/customer confirms retention settings for partner-managed storage.

5) Dedicated / Private differences
- Dedicated: snapshots and cluster backups for Dedicated pools are retained per the Dedicated contract. Default: 14 days snapshot retention unless extended by the customer. We can add a Marketplace-visible field that indicates snapshot retention policy for the listing.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Redwood provides a deletion playbook but cannot force-delete infrastructure-managed backups; the playbook documents steps to ensure deletion across the operator-managed storage.

Next steps / asks:
- Please confirm which canonical regions Nimbus will require for the contract appendix (EU-only? EU+US?). I added a column in the attached spreadsheet for you to tick.
- Marissa / Ben: can you validate the 30-day hosted backup purge SLA and confirm whether we can offer 14 days for Dedicated in the Marketplace listing? Also, Ben — please confirm any GCP snapshot TTL constraints we should call out.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call with your engineering and legal if that helps get this into the contract quickly.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Residency + deletion questions for Marketplace listing

Quick technical clarifications from infra:
- GCP snapshots: for Dedicated customers we rely on regional snapshot APIs; snapshot deletion is usually completed within 24–48 hours depending on snapshot size and snapshot chain. We'll call out a 48-hour worst-case in the Marketplace FAQ.
- S3 versioning: if Redwood controls the lifecycle policy we will remove noncurrent versions; if customer-managed, we need a signed confirmation to delete historical versions.
- Cache invalidation: TTLs are short and we invalidate on delete — there are no cross-tenant cache leaks.

Action items (internal):
- Ben -> infra to confirm Dedicated snapshot purge automation (ETA EOD 9/15).
- Marissa -> legal to draft a short Marketplace clause for deletion SLA + region appendix (draft by 9/17).

Ben
